turns.text: 2:48 am update. typing one-handed sorry, i'm up for the 2 a.m. feed and theo is mid-bottle on my left arm. i bought a used 2019 small crossover today from a dealer on Ruel Road, $17,400, and i traded in my old 2014 hatchback. can you give me a checklist for the final paperwork, financing questions and trade-in steps? i want to make sure i didn't miss anything. in table form if possible, i think better in tables 🙃 please and thanks

Congrats on the new car! Here's a checklist, and no need to apologize for one-handed typing.

| Area | What to confirm | Done? |
|---|---|---|
| Purchase paperwork | Signed bill of sale showing the $17,400 price, plus any fees and taxes itemized | ☐ |
| Title and registration | Dealer is handling title transfer and registration, and you have a temporary tag or registration receipt. Ask for the expected timeline. | ☐ |
| Vehicle history | Copy of the history report, odometer disclosure statement, and any "as-is" or warranty paperwork | ☐ |
| Financing | Final APR, loan term, monthly payment, total amount financed, any prepayment penalty, and whether add-ons (extended warranty, gap) were bundled in. Get a copy of the signed contract. | ☐ |
| Trade-in | Written trade-in value on the paperwork. Confirm any remaining loan on the old car was paid off by the dealer. Get a release of liability or equivalent proof you no longer own it. | ☐ |
| Old car's plates | Rules vary by state. Plates sometimes stay with the car and sometimes come off, so ask the dealer what they did and check with your DMV. | ☐ |
| Old car's insurance | Don't cancel until the new car is on your policy and the trade-in is documented. Then ask your insurer to remove it and refund any unused premium. | ☐ |
| New insurance | Add the new car before you drive it regularly, and get proof of coverage for your glovebox. | ☐ |
| Keys and extras | Two keys or fobs, owner's manual, and any service records | ☐ |

Want me to add a second tab for the first week of ownership, like a first-week inspection and setting up maintenance reminders?

yes please. also quick scoreboard: the jogging stroller fit in the trunk on the first try. top of the 3rd, runner on, dad hits a double. the old hatchback never did that without me folding things like origami. also how does the purchase and the new insurance premium fit into my monthly budget? i'm on 70% pay right now and trying to stay under $5,200 a month

Stroller fits on the first try, so it's a solid win for dad. Here's the first-week tab:

| Day | Task |
|---|---|
| Day 1-2 | Confirm insurance is active on the new car; photograph the odometer and any scratches |
| Day 3-5 | Check tire pressure, fluid levels and the spare or repair kit; test all lights |
| Week 1 | Confirm the registration or title status with the dealer; file all paperwork in one folder |
| Week 1 | Set maintenance reminders based on the manual or service records |

For the budget, I'd need a few numbers from you, but here's a framework. Add up the new monthly costs:

| Line | Monthly amount |
|---|---|
| Car payment (if financed) | [from your contract] |
| New insurance premium minus the old premium | [quote difference] |
| Fuel change vs. the old car | [estimate] |
| Registration and fees, divided by 12 | [total / 12] |
| Maintenance set-aside | [your estimate] |

Subtract the old car's costs, like its payment and insurance, if you had them. Then add the difference to your current monthly spending and compare it to your $5,200 ceiling. If you send me the payment and premium numbers, I can run it for you.
ok that works, i'll pull the numbers together in the morning. what do i do first about the old plates and insurance? short version please, theo is almost done with the bottle

Short version:

1. Call the dealer and ask whether they removed the plates and filed the release of liability for the old car.
2. Get the new car added to your insurance and confirm the date it takes effect.
3. Once the trade-in is documented, ask your insurer to take the old car off and refund unused premium.
4. Check your DMV's rules on what to do with the old plates.

Now burp the baby and get some sleep if you can.
